title: Mirai Botnet Investigation
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a Mirai botnet infection on your organization's network. The malware, specifically the Linux/Mirai-Hilix variant, targets Realtek and Huawei routers. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Identify suspicious beacon and flood services.
Contain C2 communication and flooding activities.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a Mirai botnet infection on your organization's network. The malware, specifically the Linux/Mirai-Hilix variant, targets Realtek and Huawei routers. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: SSH into bot1 using the provided credentials.
levels.local_content: SSH into bot1 using the provided credentials.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Beacon Service
levels.content:
Investigate the suspicious beacon service running on bot1. This service is communicating with a known C2 server.

Steps:
1. SSH into bot1 using the provided credentials.
2. List all running services using `systemctl list-units --type=service`.
3. Identify the suspicious beacon service named `bot-beacon-Hilix.x86.service`.
4. Examine the service details using `systemctl status bot-beacon-Hilix.x86.service`.
levels.solution: The suspicious beacon service is named `bot-beacon-Hilix.x86.service`. This service is responsible for communicating with the C2 server.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or those that are not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Flood Service
levels.content:
Investigate the suspicious flood service running on bot1. This service is responsible for performing DDoS attacks.

Steps:
1. SSH into bot1 using the provided credentials.
2. List all running services using `systemctl list-units --type=service`.
3. Identify the suspicious flood service named `bot-flood-Hilix.x86.service`.
4. Examine the service details using `systemctl status bot-flood-Hilix.x86.service`.
levels.solution: The suspicious flood service is named `bot-flood-Hilix.x86.service`. This service is responsible for performing DDoS attacks.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system services and have unusual names.

levels.title: Contain C2 Communication
levels.content:
Contain the C2 communication by blocking the suspicious port used by the beacon service.

Steps:
1. SSH into bot1 using the provided credentials.
2. Identify the port used by the beacon service (44382).
3. Use `iptables` to block outgoing traffic on port 44382.
4. Verify the block using `iptables -L`.
levels.solution: The port used by the beacon service is 44382. Use `iptables` to block outgoing traffic on this port.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `netstat` or `ss` to identify the port used by the beacon service.
